arxiv-2109-11361.title: Optimal Control via Combined Inference and Numerical Optimization
arxiv-2109-11361.creator: Daniel Layeghi, Steve Tonneau, Michael Mistry
arxiv-2109-11361.description: Abstract Derivative based optimization methods are efficient at solving optimal control problems near local optima. However, their ability to converge halts when derivative information vanishes. The inference approach to optimal control does not have strict requirements on the objective landscape. However, sampling, the primary tool for solving such problems, tends to be much slower in computation time.

arxiv-2203-14406.title: Active Phase for Activated Random Walk on ℤ 2 \mathbb{Z}^{2}
arxiv-2203-14406.creator: Yiping Hu
arxiv-2203-14406.description: Abstract We show that for small enough sleep rate, the critical density of the symmetric Activated Random Walk model on ℤ 2 \mathbb{Z}^{2} is strictly less than one. 1 Introduction The Activated Random Walk (ARW) model is a system of interacting particles, which is believed to exhibit self-organized criticality.

arxiv-2205-06700.title: Multi-particle Lagrangian statistics in homogeneous rotating turbulence
arxiv-2205-06700.creator: Juan Ignacio Polanco, S. Arun, Aurore Naso
arxiv-2205-06700.description: Abstract Geophysical flows are often turbulent and subject to rotation. This rotation modifies the structure of turbulence and is thereby expected to sensibly affect its Lagrangian properties. Here, we investigate the relative dispersion and geometry of pairs, triads and tetrads in homogeneous rotating turbulence, by using direct numerical simulations at different rotation rates.

arxiv-2206-06303.title: Regulating dynamics through intermittent interactions
arxiv-2206-06303.creator: Shiva Dixit, Manaoj Aravind, P. Parmananda
arxiv-2206-06303.description: Abstract In this letter, we experimentally demonstrate an efficient scheme to regulate the behaviour of coupled nonlinear oscillators through dynamic control of their interaction. It is observed that introducing intermittency in the interaction term as a function of time or the system state, predictably alters the dynamics of the constituent oscillators.

arxiv-2305-06433.title: Inverse projection of axisymmetric orientation distributions
arxiv-2305-06433.creator: Philipp A. Kloza, James A. Elliott
arxiv-2305-06433.description: Abstract We show that the projection of an axisymmetric three-dimensional orientation distribution to two dimensions can be cast into an Abel transform. Based on this correspondence, we derive an exact integral inverse, which allows for the quantification of three-dimensional uniaxial alignment of rod-like units from two-dimensional sliced images, thus providing an alternative to X-ray or tomographic analysis.

arxiv-2311-13555.title: The transient IDEMIX model as a nonorographic gravity wave parameterization in an atmospheric circulation model
arxiv-2311-13555.description: Abstract The Internal wave Dissipation, Energy and Mixing (IDEMIX) model presents a novel way of parameterizing internal gravity waves in the atmosphere. Using a continuous full wave spectrum in the energy balance equation and integrating over all vertical wavenumbers and frequencies results in prognostic equations for the energy density of gravity waves in multiple azimuthal compartments.

arxiv-2401-14868.title: Particle-MALA and Particle-mGRAD: Gradient-based MCMC methods for high-dimensional state-space models
arxiv-2401-14868.creator: Adrien Corenflos, Axel Finke
arxiv-2401-14868.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Adrien Corenflos, Axel Finke. State-of-the-art methods for Bayesian inference in state-space models are (a) conditional sequential Monte Carlo (CSMC) algorithms; (b) sophisticated ‘classical’ MCMC algorithms like MALA , or mGRAD from Titsias and Papaspiliopoulos, 2018 . The former propose N N particles at each time step to exploit the model’s ‘decorrelation-over-time’ property and thus scale favourably with the time horizon, T T , but break down if the dimension of the latent states, D D , is large.

arxiv-2402-08189.title: Simulating Strategic Reasoning: Comparing the Ability of Single LLMs and Multi-Agent Systems to Replicate Human Behavior
arxiv-2402-08189.creator: Karthik Sreedhar, Lydia Chilton
arxiv-2402-08189.description: Abstract When creating policies, plans, or designs for people, it is challenging for designers to foresee all of the ways in which people may reason and behave. Recently, Large Language Models (LLMs) have been shown to be able to simulate human reasoning.

arxiv-2403-19722.title: Satellite Visibility During the April 2024 Total Eclipse This research was made possible by the open-source projects Skyfield ( Rhodes 2019 ) , REBOUND ( Rein & Liu 2012 ) , Jupyter ( Kluyver et al. 2016 ) , iPython ( Pérez & Granger 2007 ) , and matplotlib ( Hunter 2007 ) .
arxiv-2403-19722.creator: Samantha M. Lawler, Hanno Rein, Aaron C. Boley
arxiv-2403-19722.description: Abstract On 8 April 2024, tens of millions of people across North America will be able to view a total solar eclipse. Such astronomical events have been important throughout history, but with nearly 10,000 satellites in orbit, we question whether total eclipses will now reveal a sky full of satellites, fundamentally changing this experience for humanity.

arxiv-2405-20588.title: DAFNet: Dynamic Auxiliary Fusion for Sequential Model Editing in Large Language Models
arxiv-2405-20588.creator: Taolin Zhang, Qizhou Chen, Dongyang Li, Chengyu Wang, Xiaofeng He, Longtao Huang, Hui Xue, Jun Huang
arxiv-2405-20588.description: Abstract Recently, while large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated impressive results, they still suffer from hallucination, i.e., the generation of false information. Model editing is the task of fixing factual mistakes in LLMs; yet, most previous works treat it as a one-time task, paying little attention to ever-emerging mistakes generated by LLMs.

arxiv-2411-08732.title: Quantitative imaging of the fresh/saltwater interface with airborne electromagnetics: examining different sources of uncertainty
arxiv-2411-08732.creator: Wouter Deleersnyder 1,2 , David Dudal 1 , Thomas Hermans 2 1 KU Leuven Campus Kortrijk - KULAK, Department of Physics, Etienne Sabbelaan 53, 8500 Kortrijk, Belgium. 2 Ghent University, Department of Geology, Krijgslaan 281 - S8, 9000 Gent, Belgium E-mail: wouter.deleersnyder@ugent.be
arxiv-2411-08732.description: Abstract Knowing the distribution between fresh and saline groundwater is imperative for sustainable and integrated management of water resources in coastal areas. The airborne electromagnetic (AEM) method is increasingly used for hydrogeological mapping over large areas via bulk electrical resistivity. However, accurately and reliably mapping the fresh/saltwater interface (FSI) requires accurate knowledge about the transition zone.

arxiv-2501-12799.title: Int2Planner: An Intention-based Multi-modal Motion Planner for Integrated Prediction and Planning
arxiv-2501-12799.creator: Xiaolei Chen, Junchi Yan, Wenlong Liao, Tao He, Pai Peng
arxiv-2501-12799.description: Abstract Motion planning is a critical module in autonomous driving, with the primary challenge of uncertainty caused by interactions with other participants. As most previous methods treat prediction and planning as separate tasks, it is difficult to model these interactions.

arxiv-2506-15119.title: Definability of complex functions in o-minimal structures
arxiv-2506-15119.creator: Adele Padgett, Patrick Speissegger
arxiv-2506-15119.description: Abstract . We prove that some holomorphic continuations of functions in the classes 𝐚𝐧 ∗ \mathbf{an}^{*} and 𝒢 \mathcal{G} are definable in the o-minimal structures ℝ an ∗ \mathbb{R}_{\an^{*}} and ℝ 𝒢 \mathbb{R}_{\mathcal{G}} respectively. More specifically, we give complex domains on which the holomorphic continuations are definable, and show they are optimal.

arxiv-2509-14393.title: Ideally Connected Cographs and Chordal Graphs
arxiv-2509-14393.creator: Richter Jordaan
arxiv-2509-14393.description: Abstract For distinct vertices u , v u,v in a graph G G , let κ G ​ ( u , v ) \kappa_{G}(u,v) denote the maximum number of internally disjoint u u - v v paths in G G .

arxiv-2509-19804.title: DynaFlow: Dynamics-embedded Flow Matching for Physically Consistent Motion Generation from State-only Demonstrations
arxiv-2509-19804.creator: Sowoo Lee, Dongyun Kang, Jaehyun Park, Hae-Won Park
arxiv-2509-19804.description: Abstract This paper introduces DynaFlow, a novel framework that embeds a differentiable simulator directly into a flow matching model. By generating trajectories in the action space and mapping them to dynamically feasible state trajectories via the simulator, DynaFlow ensures all outputs are physically consistent by construction.

arxiv-2509-25717.title: Importance Sampling for Multi-Negative Multimodal Direct Preference Optimization
arxiv-2509-25717.creator: Xintong Li, Chuhan Wang, Junda Wu, Rohan Surana, Tong Yu, Julian McAuley, Jingbo Shang
arxiv-2509-25717.description: Abstract Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) has recently been extended from text-only models to vision-language models. However, existing methods rely on oversimplified pairwise comparisons, generating a single negative image via basic perturbations or similarity-based retrieval, which fail to capture the complex nature of multimodal preferences, inducing optimization bias and hallucinations.

arxiv-2512-14366.title: Optimizing Rank for High-Fidelity Implicit Neural Representations
arxiv-2512-14366.creator: Julian McGinnis, Florian A. Hölzl, Suprosanna Shit, Florentin Bieder, Paul Friedrich, Mark Mühlau, Björn Menze, Daniel Rueckert, Benedikt Wiestler
arxiv-2512-14366.description: Abstract Implicit Neural Representations (INRs) based on vanilla Multi-Layer Perceptrons (MLPs) are widely believed to be incapable of representing high-frequency content. This has directed research efforts towards architectural interventions, such as coordinate embeddings or specialized activation functions, to represent high-frequency signals.

europmc-pmc8160230.creator: Jarczak D, Kluge S, Nierhaus A.
europmc-pmc8160230.description: Sepsis is a life-threatening condition and a global disease burden. Today, the heterogeneous syndrome is defined as severe organ dysfunction caused by a dysregulated host response to infection, with renewed emphasis on immune pathophysiology. Despite all efforts of experimental...

plos-pbio-0020239.creator: Michael J Galko, Mark A Krasnow
plos-pbio-0020239.description: PLOS ONE research article. To establish a genetic system to study postembryonic wound healing, we characterized epidermal wound healing in Drosophila larvae. Following puncture wounding, larvae begin to bleed but within an hour a plug forms in the wound gap. Over the next couple of hours the outer part of

pmc-10665962.title: Experimental study on influence of particle shape on shockwave from collapse of cavitation bubble
pmc-10665962.creator: Lingtao Zou, Jing Luo, Weilin Xu, Yanwei Zhai, Jie Li, Tong Qu, Guihua Fu
pmc-10665962.description: The bubble dynamics under the influence of particles is an unavoidable issue in many cavitation applications, with a fundamental aspect being the shockwave affected by particles during bubble collapse. In our experiments, the method of spark-induced bubbles was used, while a high-speed camera and a piezoresistive pressure sensor were utilized to investigate how particle shape affects the evolution of shockwaves.

pmc-11285266.title: Exploring the wound-healing potential and seasonal chemical variability of the Formosan Callery pear Pyrus calleryana: implications for therapeutic applications
pmc-11285266.creator: Bo-Rong Peng, Xin-Yun Tang, Yun-Shiuan Chen, Kuei-Hung Lai, Mei-Hsien Lee
pmc-11285266.description: ContextPyrus calleryana Decne (Rosaceae), renowned for its therapeutic properties, is known to moisturize the lungs (removing dryness; relieving cough), clear heat (acting as an antipyretic; febrifuge) and aid in detoxification (relieving pyogenic inflammation; eliminating toxins). However, scientific evidence supporting its efficacy in wound healing is lacking.ObjectiveThis study investigated P.

pmc-11352139.title: A Hunt for the Resistance of Haemophilus influnezae to Beta-Lactams
pmc-11352139.creator: Mélanie Denizon, Eva Hong, Aude Terrade, Muhamed-Kheir Taha, Ala-Eddine Deghmane, Krisztina M Papp-Wallace
pmc-11352139.description: Infections due to Haemophilus influnezae require prompt treatment using beta-lactam antibiotics. We used a collection of 81 isolates obtained between 1940 and 2001 from several countries. Whole genome sequencing showed the high heterogeneity of these isolates but allowed us to track the acquisition of beta-lactamase, which was first detected in 1980.

pmc-11424823.title: Exploring vision transformers for classifying early Barrett's dysplasia in endoscopic images: A pilot study on white‐light and narrow‐band imaging
pmc-11424823.creator: Jin L Tan, Dileepa Pitawela, Mohamed A Chinnaratha, Andrawus Beany, Enrik J Aguila, Hsiang‐Ting Chen, Gustavo Carneiro, Rajvinder Singh
pmc-11424823.description: Background and AimVarious deep learning models, based on convolutional neural network (CNN), have been shown to improve the detection of early esophageal neoplasia in Barrett's esophagus. Vision transformer (ViT), derived from natural language processing, has emerged as the new state‐of‐the‐art for image recognition, outperforming predecessors such as CNN.

pmc-11706596.title: Comparative analysis of cancer statistics in China and the United States in 2024
pmc-11706596.creator: Yujie Wu, Siyi He, Mengdi Cao, Yi Teng, Qianru Li, Nuopei Tan, Jiachen Wang, Tingting Zuo, Tianyi Li, Yuanjie Zheng, Changfa Xia, Wanqing Chen
pmc-11706596.description: Background:Cancer patterns in China are becoming similar to those in the United States (US). Comparing the recent cancer profiles, trends, and determinants in China and the US can provide useful reference data.Methods:This study used open-source data. We used GLOBOCAN 2022 cancer estimates and United Nations population estimates to calculate cancer cases and deaths in both countries during 2024.

pmc-12418706.title: Intestinal epithelial Dicer1 regulates gut microbiome and Alzheimer’s pathology in App-knock-in mice
pmc-12418706.creator: Wenlin Hao, Qinghua Luo, Ilona Magdalena Szabo, Gilles Gasparoni, Sascha Tierling, Wenqiang Quan, Hsin-Fang Chang, Gang Wu, Julia Schulze-Hentrich, Yang Liu
pmc-12418706.description: BackgroundAlzheimer’s disease (AD) patients and animal models exhibit an altered gut microbiome that is associated with pathological changes in the brain. Intestinal miRNA enters bacteria and regulates bacterial metabolism and proliferation. This study aimed to investigate whether the manipulation of miRNA could alter the gut microbiome and AD pathologies.

pmc-12520108.title: The space-time continuum in neurological disorders of the autophagosome-lysosome fusion machinery
pmc-12520108.creator: Hormos Salimi Dafsari, Juliane Schuler, Emil Schober, Birk Möller, Adam Antebi, Manolis Fanto, Heinz Jungbluth
pmc-12520108.description: Autophagy is a highly conserved cellular pathway for the degradation and recycling of defective intracellular cargo and plays a vital role in the homeostasis of post-mitotic tissues, particularly the nervous system. Autophagosome-lysosome fusion represents the final critical step in macroautophagy with a tightly regulated process mediated by a complex molecular machinery of tethering vesicles for degradation.

pmc-12638672.title: Providencia rettgeri as an unusual pathogen in diabetic foot osteomyelitis: A case report and literature review
pmc-12638672.creator: Stephanie N Campbell, Madeleine Mehaffey, Nikita Gambhir, Amanda L Killeen
pmc-12638672.description: Providencia rettgeri is a Gram-negative bacterium, rarely reported as a cause of diabetic wound infections. Its frequent resistance to β-lactams and carbapenems limits treatment options, especially in immunocompromised patients. We present the case of a 59-year-old unhoused male living with diabetes, peripheral artery disease, and prior bilateral transmetatarsal amputations who presented with a University of Texas 3B diabetic foot ulcer.

pmc-13139510.title: Dual-branch attention network with deep split convolution and multi-dimensional transformers for medical image segmentation
pmc-13139510.creator: Debao Li, Cheng Yuan, Yexiang Yao, Yongqiang Qiu, Haobo Yin
pmc-13139510.description: While the segmentation of anatomical structures and pathological regions is indispensable for reliable disease assessment, contemporary algorithms often fail to achieve sharp demarcation. This deficiency stems from the high degree of morphological heterogeneity across different cases, which results in obscured contours and compromised segmentation accuracy.

pmc-13272231.title: Exploring the relationship between retinal damage and cognition in multiple sclerosis: a cross-sectional OCT-MRI study
pmc-13272231.creator: Riccardo Maria Borgo, Manuela Altieri, Alessandro Pasquale De Rosa, Rocco Capuano, Alvino Bisecco, Fabrizio Esposito, Alessandro Tessitore, Alessandro d’Ambrosio, Antonio Gallo

pmc-13512188.title: Tympanic Membrane Involvement of Multiple Myeloma: Report of a Case
pmc-13512188.creator: Elisavet Manaki, Antri Polyviou, Sosana Delimpasi, Mathilde Chroni, Ioannis Vlastos
pmc-13512188.description: Extramedullary Involvement (EMI) in Multiple Myeloma (MM) is a rare but aggressive entity that usually occurs in advanced or relapsed cases of MM. Although otologic manifestations aren’t frequent, they may mimic common inflammatory or neoplastic pathologies and could be a diagnostic challenge for the clinician.

pmc-13624706.title: Five‐Year CT‐Based Skeletal Muscle Decline Curves in Cirrhosis According to Liver Functional Reserve and Routinely Available Clinical Factors
pmc-13624706.creator: Suguru Miida, Hiroteru Kamimura, Hitoshi Yoshiji, Masahito Shimizu, Takumi Kawaguchi, Tetsuya Tsuji, Saori Endo, Hiroki Natsui, Hiroki Maruyama, Hiroyuki Abe, Tadashi Namisaki, Takao Miwa

pmc-13626894.title: External validation of predictive equations for determining the need for in-flight oxygen supplementation in patients with respiratory disease
pmc-13626894.creator: Murielle Emma Beaupré, Gao Sheng Huang, Bruno-Pierre Dubé
pmc-13626894.description: RationalePatients with chronic respiratory diseases may develop clinically significant hypoxemia during commercial air travel because of reduced cabin pressure. In-flight oxygen prescription is typically guided by hypoxic challenge testing (HCT), a procedure that is time-consuming, costly, and not universally available. Several predictive equations based on sea-level physiological measurements have been proposed as alternatives.

pmc-13640083.title: A novel preclinical strategy for diabetic wound: CITED2-loaded hydrogel spray targeted macrophage reprogramming
pmc-13640083.creator: Xichao Jian, Jingjie Shao, Shihan Tang, Xing Hu, Qi He, Miaomiao Wei, Yaping Deng, Yan Zhou, Shune Xiao, Fang Qi, Chengliang Deng
pmc-13640083.description: Diabetic wounds resent a considerable clinical challenge due to impaired healing, which results from persistent inflammation and dysregulated macrophage polarization. This study identifies CITED2 as a critical regulator of diabetic wound repair, primarily through its role in modulating macrophage plasticity.
